name: Sinan ibn Abu Harithah
bio: Sinan ibn Abu Harithah was a chief of the branch of Murrah descended from Ghaidh, of Dhubyan. Lyall notes that he is the man to whom the young prince of al-Hirah, slain by al-Harith ibn Dhalim, was entrusted for education.
Two pieces by him are in the Mufaddaliyat.

poems.title: Ode C: Say to al-Muthallam and Malik son
poems.author: Sinan ibn Abu Harithah
poems.note: Lyall's heading: Sinan son of Abu Harithah, of Murrah, of Dhubyan.
poems.text:
Say to al-Muthallam and Malik son of Hind — ' If thou desirest to assail our strength, come on !

' Thou shalt find among us what our enemies have to face, and thou shalt be given a morning draught from a cup the dregs of which are bitter as colocynth.

' We will present to the [enemy's] troop, what time the spears meet in conflict, a thrust like the blazing of a flaming fire.

' Of us are horsemen in Shajnah, and adh-Dhinab, and 'Uta'id, like the blackness of thick darkness ;

' And in Darghad and on as-Sudairah are they ready, and in Dhu Amarr, where their women-kind have never been divided as spoil [among a victorious foe] '.

poems.title: Ode CI: If now I complain not to
poems.author: Sinan ibn Abu Harithah
poems.text:
If now I complain not to any of my pain, and if I cannot direct my steps unless I have one to guide me,

Yet time was when I have brought at dawn upon the pasturing camels of a tribe a host of raiders, far-spreading, one following another, besetting them suddenly from lowland and upland alike ;

And time was that I have taken my part in the arrow-game when the milk-less camels were driven home at evening by the cold, rain joined with chilling wind :

Then was I wont to give of my provision, without reserve, to all the folk of the encampment, whether protected strangers or seekers for bounty.

And time was that I prevented, without causing injury to any, a breach in the tribe — yea, all my equals in age are my witnesses !

Well do my people know how, when their long-continued raid has carried them far, and they have spent all their provision, I have lavished upon them all of mine.

And I do not hide within me qualities for which I shall be reviled — no, not till the son of Mayyad return again from the grave !

Give me praise ! How many a door of noble deeds prepared for you, how many a valley [leading thereto], have I opened to you !
